text: `parseDigits` returns `NaN` when the string has no parseable digits. It first tries `parseInt(str, 10)`; if that is NaN it walks the string converting Han decimal characters and any of the supported non-Latin digit ranges (arab, deva, thai, ...) into Latin digits, then returns `parseInt(value, 10)` — and since `value` is `""` when nothing matched, that final `parseInt("")` yields `NaN`. So `parseDigits("abc")`, `parseDigits("")`, `parseDigits("P1Y")` all give `NaN`, while e.g. `parseDigits("12")` gives `12`.

It returns the pair `[matches, {}]` — i.e. `[null, {}]`, since `matches` is the (null) result of `input.match(regex)`. The empty object is the parsed-values map, so callers get a falsy `matches` and no values.

It returns `unitOutOfRange("weekYear", obj.weekYear)` — i.e. an `Invalid` instance (truthy, not a boolean `true`), since `isInteger(obj.weekYear)` fails and that branch is taken first. Callers treat a truthy return as "invalid" and use it as the invalid reason.

Fixed and verified. `Interval.fromISO` now parses the two halves defensively (try/catch around `DateTime.fromISO`), so under `Settings.throwOnInvalid` the duration forms (`<start>/<duration>`, `<duration>/<end>`) return a valid Interval instead of throwing `InvalidDateTimeError`, while genuinely unparsable input still throws `InvalidIntervalError`. Checked: "2007-03-01T13:00:00/P1Y2M10DT2H30M", "P1Y2M10DT2H30M/2008-05-11T15:30:00", "2016-01-01/P1Y", "P1Y/2016-01-01" all valid; "hello", "foo/bar", "" still throw. Full test suite: no regressions.

Fixed and verified. In `src/impl/util.js`, `objToLocalTS` reverted the 19XX legacy-year interpretation with `d.setUTCFullYear(d.getUTCFullYear() - 1900)`, which normalized day/month overflow against year 2000 (a leap year) instead of year 100 (not a leap year). It now uses `d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)`, so the overflow is normalized against the real year. E.g. `DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ days: 61 })` is now `0100-03-02` (was `0100-03-01`); the existing 100-barrier tests still pass. Full suite: no regressions.

Fixed and verified. `DateTime#isInDST` compared against `this.set({ month: 1 })`, which keeps the day-of-month; for years with year-round DST (1974 USA) January 6th onward is itself DST, so the comparison collapsed and isInDST flipped to false for every day >= 6. It now compares against `this.set({ month: 1, day: 1 })` (standard time). Verified for America/New_York 1974: false Jan 1-5, true Jan 6 through Oct 26, false Oct 27 (DST ended 2am that day) onward. Existing LA pre/during/post-DST tests still pass; full suite: no regressions.

Fixed and verified. In `src/duration.js` the conversion matrices were missing two entries, so `normalize()` produced NaN for some unit pairs: `years.quarters` was absent in both the casual and longterm matrices, and `quarters.seconds` was absent from the casual matrix. Added `quarters: 4` to `years` in both matrices and `seconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60` to casual `quarters`. All 36 unit pairs now normalize without NaN and without changing the duration's value (checked for both conversion accuracies and several magnitudes/signs); existing normalize tests still pass.

It sets the internal `defaultZone` to `null` (`if (!z) { defaultZone = null; } else { defaultZone = normalizeZone(z); }`), so the default zone falls back to the system local zone via the `defaultZone` getter (`defaultZone || LocalZone.instance`).
It's an abstract getter on the `Zone` base class: it just throws `ZoneIsAbstractError` (it must be overridden by concrete zones, which return a string like "system", "iana", "fixed" or "invalid").

Fixed and verified. `padStart` in `src/impl/util.js` padded by slicing the stringified number, so a negative year put the minus sign inside the padding: year -1 formatted as `00-1`. It now pads the absolute value and re-attaches the sign. `DateTime.fromObject({ year: -1, month: 5, day: 25, zone: "utc" }).toISODate()` is now `-0001-05-25` (was `00-1-05-25`); -10 → `-0010-05-25`, -100 → `-0100-05-25`, and the existing ±118040 and positive-year cases are unchanged. Full suite: no regressions.

It returns a `FixedOffsetZone` built from the parsed offset: `zone = new FixedOffsetZone(matches.Z)` (where `matches.Z` is the offset in minutes). If `matches.Z` is undefined it falls back to `matches.z` → `IANAZone.create(matches.z)`, otherwise `null`. The function returns the pair `[vals, zone]`.

Hour 24 is valid only when the rest of the time is exactly midnight: `hour === 24 && minute === 0 && second === 0 && millisecond === 0` (the `validHour` check is `integerBetween(hour, 0, 23) || (hour === 24 && minute === 0 && second === 0 && millisecond === 0)`). So `24:00:00.000` is accepted (as ISO 8601 allows) while e.g. `24:00:01` is "unit out of range".

Fixed and verified. `FixedOffsetZone#isValid` was hard-coded to `true`, so a zone constructed with a non-numeric offset (e.g. `new FixedOffsetZone("foo")`, `undefined`, `null`, or `NaN`) claimed to be valid and DateTimes built with it were not flagged. It now returns `isNumber(this.fixed) && !Number.isNaN(this.fixed)`. Verified: non-numeric/undefined/null/NaN offsets → `isValid === false`; numeric offsets (0, 60, -330), `utcInstance` and `instance(n)` → `true`; `DateTime.fromObject({...}, { zone: new FixedOffsetZone("foo") })` is now invalid with reason "unsupported zone" (was a bogus valid DateTime). Existing fixed-offset behaviour (names, `parseSpecifier`, `fromISO`/`fromFormat`/`fromRFC2822` offsets, `setZone("UTC+6")`, `toUTC`) is unchanged and the full suite still shows only the 2 pre-existing failures.
